Password, user name, URIs and host names are masked; no e-mail addresses or GUIDs were present.
Data-plane only: no cluster configuration was changed.

conclusions.question: Are collection validators (validator / validationLevel / validationAction) enabled on the managed service, or gated behind CommandNotSupported 'validator not supported yet'?
conclusions.answer: Enabled on this cluster with no enablement step. create and collMod both accept a baseline $jsonSchema (bsonType/required/properties) with ok: 1; listCollections shows the validator with validationLevel 'strict' and validationAction 'error'; violating inserts, updates and findAndModify are rejected. The cluster resource has no previewFeatures property and has never been modified (lastModifiedAt = createdAt 2026-11-25T20:35:33Z). The words 'not supported yet' appeared in no response; the only 'not supported' wording was 'The '<keyword>' keyword in $jsonSchema is not supported at this time' for $schema and format, and 'The 'integer' type in $jsonSchema is not supported at this time.' (all code 9 FailedToParse).

conclusions.question: Which $jsonSchema keywords do create and collMod accept on the managed service?
conclusions.answer: enum and oneOf: accepted by create and collMod and enforced (valid docs inserted, violating docs rejected with 121), also after collMod. additionalProperties (also with _id declared in properties), allOf, anyOf, not, patternProperties, dependencies, minProperties and maxProperties: rejected identically by create and collMod with code 9 FailedToParse 'Unknown $jsonSchema keyword: <keyword>' and no errorLabels. The $jsonSchema query operator in find accepts and rejects exactly the same set, and for baseline, enum and oneOf it matched only the valid document, as MongoDB would. So Learn's $jsonSchema page (which lists enum and oneOf as unsupported) is stale for this managed build, and the engine-source dispatch list in DECISIONS topic 10 matches the managed service.

conclusions.question: What does a write that violates a validator return (code, codeName, message, errInfo, labels)?
conclusions.answer: insert and update: ok: 1 with writeErrors[0] = {index, code: 121, errmsg: 'Document failed validation'}: no codeName, no errInfo (so no MongoDB 5.0-style errInfo.details explaining which rule failed) and no errorLabels; PyMongo insert_one raises WriteError code 121 with those details. findAndModify: command error ok: 0, code 121, codeName 'DocumentFailedValidation', same errmsg, no errInfo. MongoDB's codeName for 121 is 'DocumentValidationFailure'; the managed name matches the open-source gateway's error_mappings.csv entry '121,DocumentFailedValidation', so code that matches on codeName must use the code 121 instead. The insert shape matches open-source 0.117 exactly; update and findAndModify were not run there.

conclusions.question: Do bypassDocumentValidation, validationAction 'warn' and collMod-attached validators behave as in MongoDB?
conclusions.answer: Yes on this cluster: bypassDocumentValidation: true on insert lets a violating document through (n=1); a collection created with validationAction 'warn' accepts a violating insert (n=1); a validator attached by collMod to an existing collection is enforced on the next insert (121). The bypass result matches open-source 0.117; warn and collMod enforcement were not run there.

conclusions.question: Extra (beyond the spec list): are title/description, $schema, format and type 'integer' accepted?
conclusions.answer: title and description (top level and on a property) are accepted and the validator still enforces required, although Learn lists them as unsupported. $schema and format are rejected with 9 FailedToParse 'The '$schema' keyword in $jsonSchema is not supported at this time' / 'The 'format' keyword in $jsonSchema is not supported at this time'; type 'integer' is rejected with 9 FailedToParse 'The 'integer' type in $jsonSchema is not supported at this time.' (MongoDB also omits these three). Generated JSON Schemas (for example from Pydantic or zod) must be stripped of $schema and format and use bsonType 'int'/'long' instead of type 'integer'.

conclusions.question: Is a unique index with partialFilterExpression { key: { $exists: true } } accepted and enforced?
conclusions.answer: Accepted: createIndexes returns ok: 1 with numIndexesBefore 1 / numIndexesAfter 2 nested under raw.defaultShard; listIndexes shows the spec verbatim plus storageEngine.enableOrderedIndex: true. A duplicate {key:1} fails with write error 11000 'Duplicate key violation on the requested collection: Index 'uq_key_exists'' (no codeName, no keyPattern/keyValue). Two documents without the key both insert; two explicit {key:null} documents collide (second fails 11000), so null is inside the $exists:true filter as in MongoDB. 4 documents stored.

conclusions.question: Is a unique index with partialFilterExpression { key: { $gt: 0 } } accepted and enforced?
conclusions.answer: Accepted (numIndexesAfter 2). A duplicate {key:5} fails with 11000; duplicates of {key:0}, {key:-1}, a missing key and {key:'s'} all insert (outside the numeric filter; strings are type-bracketed out). updateOne moving {key:0} to {key:5} fails with write error 11000, so uniqueness is enforced when an update brings a document into the filter. 9 documents stored.

conclusions.question: Is $exists: false allowed in a partial filter?
conclusions.answer: No. createIndexes fails with 67 CannotCreateIndex 'Error in specification { "key" : { "key" : 1 }, "name" : "uq_key_notexists", "unique" : true, "partialFilterExpression" : { "key" : { "$exists" : false } } }:Expression not supported in partial index: key $exists false' (with a trailing newline). A non-unique partial index with $exists: false is rejected the same way (open-source only tested the unique form).

conclusions.question: Can unique + sparse be combined with partialFilterExpression?
conclusions.answer: No: 197 InvalidIndexSpecificationOption 'Error in specification { ... "sparse" : true, "partialFilterExpression" : { "key2" : { "$gt" : 0 } } }:cannot mix "partialFilterExpression" and "sparse" options'. unique + sparse without a filter is accepted and behaves as a sparse unique index: two documents without the key insert, and a duplicate value fails with 11000 (the first of an ordered pair is inserted, n=1).

conclusions.question: Where does the managed service differ from open-source 0.117 in this test?
conclusions.answer: Only in metadata: hello.maxWireVersion 25 vs 21, buildInfo.version 8.0.0 vs 7.0.0, hello.internal.documentdb_versions ['2.2-1','2.3.0','12.1-1'] with kind 'azuredocumentdb', and an extra statsEnabled: true in listCollections options. Every code, codeName, errmsg, errInfo absence and createIndexes result shape matched in all steps run on both.

conclusions.question: Is the result reproducible?
conclusions.answer: Yes. A second full run against a freshly dropped mt_schema produced identical outcomes (kind, code, codeName, errmsg, errInfo presence, n, matched) for all 92 scripted steps.

conclusions.question: What does this mean for DECISIONS topic 10 open item 1 (engine build, enum/oneOf live, validator enablement path)?
conclusions.answer: For a new cluster created 2026-11-25 in eastus (M30, server 8.0, engine documentdb_versions 2.2-1 / 2.3.0 / 12.1-1), enum and oneOf are live and collection validators need no preview flag, support request or configuration change. Filings can say validators work out of the box on current clusters, that enum and oneOf are supported, and that the remaining unsupported keywords fail with 9 FailedToParse. Whether older clusters, other regions or other server versions behave the same was not tested.
